purpose: Bound task #16's routed/shared MoE overlap experiment on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q3_K_M before any decode-graph DAG integration.
source_reference: qwen-kernel@52e240f9c6d91750d0e5e692976cfb67fd9bc603 leaves router/routed experts and the shared expert as independent branches before the layer-tail join.

hardware.cross_card_status: GPU0/W7900 was untouched; no W7900 throughput claim is made.

software.rocprof: rocprofv3 kernel trace scoped to measured eager decode with ROCTX selected regions

premise.join: The existing shared-gate/residual/next-RMS tail consumes both branch outputs.
premise.eligibility_reason: The 39 IQ3_XXS selected-dual+SiLU layers do not use ffn_gate_up, so selected and shared scratch is disjoint. Layer 39's exact fallback can reuse ffn_gate_up and remained serial.
premise.prior_serial_graph_upper_bound: The retained graph trace puts roughly 0.51 ms/token of shared gate/up + SiLU + down kernel work behind the longer routed branch, enough to justify the required eager probe but not itself evidence of overlap.

experimental_implementation.scope: uncommitted eager-only diagnostic, removed after the stop gate
experimental_implementation.main_stream: default eager stream: router -> selected gate/up -> selected down -> tail
experimental_implementation.aux_stream: one reusable nonblocking HIP stream: shared gate/up -> SiLU -> shared down
experimental_implementation.dependencies: Reusable disable-timing HIP events explicitly forked aux work after post_norm and joined it before the tail.
experimental_implementation.graph_policy: Non-default graph-capture streams deliberately stayed serial until eager overlap and >=1% full-step gates passed.
experimental_implementation.unit_gate_before_measurement: 20 passed across tests/test_hip_runtime.py and tests/test_qwen35_gguf_iq_dispatch.py; RED first failed on missing event/DAG APIs.

correctness.state_reset_note: The 16-token eager run preserved the full generated sequence, and the independent session graph smoke preserved eager/graph trajectory and final logits.

matched_eager_decode16.workload: 512 prompt tokens, 16 measured eager decode tokens, one warmup token, persistent session, native-attention row-bulk prefill, grouped raw-IQ prefill default, no GEMV decode rewrite
matched_eager_decode16.interpretation: The profiler-scoped eager wall regressed by 2.48%. Kernel work was nearly unchanged; the extra event/two-stream submission gaps expanded the trace span by 43.92 ms over 16 tokens.

timeline_stop_gate.required: Profiler-visible concurrent kernel intervals, not merely distinct stream/queue labels.
timeline_stop_gate.interpretation: HIP created two queues, but Python/ctypes submission gaps left only one kernel executing at a time. Shared work completed before the selected kernels were submitted, so the queue split did not realize device concurrency.

reasons: Zero profiler-visible kernel overlap across all 624 eligible branch pairs.
Matched 512/16 eager wall regressed 9.0261 -> 8.8077 tok/s (-2.42%), far below the required >=1% gain.
The experiment therefore failed before graph-DAG integration, repeated 512/128 and 4K/128 gates, or Q4/PARO transfer.
stop_decision.future_reopen_condition: Only a device-side/C submission design that first demonstrates overlapping real kernel timestamps without per-layer event overhead; do not retry the Python eager stream split or infer concurrency from queue IDs.

related_prior_evidence.note: A separate W7900 PARO MTP C-dispatch stream split was also exact but regressed graph-off and all-cycle graph-auto wall. It is contextual evidence, not the current GPU1 decision source.
